title: ESQL: Fix Analyzer to not interpret escaped * as a pattern

timeline.body:
Fix a bug in the Analyzer which always considered `*` (match any string)
 in field names even when escaped (back quoted). This caused the clause
 to be too greedy and either keep or drop too many fields.

Fix #104955
Pinging @elastic/es-analytical-engine (Team:Analytics)
Hi @costin, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

timeline.message:
ESQL: Fix Analyzer to not interpret escaped * as a pattern

Fix a bug in the Analyzer which always considered `*` (match any string)
 in field names even when escaped (back quoted). This caused the clause
 to be too greedy and either keep or drop too many fields.

Fix #104955
timeline.author: Costin Leau

timeline.body: CSV test that showed the previous bug - instead of matching on the name, the * acted as a wildcard.

timeline.body: Small modification to allow quoted and unquoted declarations for the name pattern.

Most of the changes here are massaging the previous code to work without an `UnresolvedAttribute`.
A bool parameter was not used and the extension was done through a supplier in order to throw an error when the pattern does not match.
The code here is somewhat messy due to String parsing...

This discovery method does a bit of heuristics on the unresolved attribute - I've modified it in place to support the new supported field however in the future it can be both improved and refactored into a separate class.
Had to modify this method as well since its pluggable mechanism was no longer suitable.
allowCompound just like `isPattern` were not needed.
Had to open the constructor up for the UnresolvedNamePattern.

timeline.author: Costin Leau

timeline.body:
I'd add the test that is reported in the bug itself:
```
row a = 1 | stats COUNT(*) | sort `count(*)`
```
Also, this PR affect the `drop` command as well. Some tests are needed there as well.

Likely a separate issue, if it's too involved to fix here:
```
row a = 0, `a*` = 1, `ab*` = 2, `ab*cd` = 3, `abc*de` = 4 | rename `ab*` as `xx*`
```

Notice that escaping used in `rename` command; still the behavior is wrong and the query generates an error message:

```
"type": "parsing_exception",
                "reason": "line 1:69: Using wildcards (*) in renaming projections is not allowed [`ab*`* as `xx*`*]",
                "stack_trace": "org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.parser.ParsingException: line 1:69: Using wildcards (*) in renaming projections is not allowed [`ab*`* as `xx*`*]
```

```suggestion
            msg += ", did you mean "
```

The message is slightly inconsistent with what we use in ql in general (`to match` is extra).

reply.body: I've done the change on purpose to signal it's a pattern not regular name matching.
